subject: Banking
title: Chinese Paper Money
description: A quick win: understand Chinese Paper Money.

hook.text: China invented paper money in the 7th century. Merchants tired of carrying heavy coins created deposit receipts instead.

buildup.text: The Song Dynasty made it official in 1024. Government-issued jiaozi became the world's first legal paper currency.

discovery.text: Paper money is a bank promise: the note represents value stored elsewhere.

twist.text: Overprinting caused inflation. The Yuan Dynasty printed so much paper money that its value collapsed entirely.

climax.text: China invented paper money and also discovered its biggest danger: print too much and trust in the currency dies.

punchline.text: China invented paper money. Then they printed too much of it.

quiz.question: When did China first issue government paper money?

details.summary: China invented paper money during the Tang Dynasty around the 7th century, centuries before it appeared in Europe. The innovation solved the problem of transporting heavy coins but also introduced the world to the problem of over-issuance and inflation.
details.whyItMatters: Paper money is the foundation of modern banking and commerce. China's early experiments showed both the power of paper currency to facilitate trade and the danger of governments printing too much of it.
takeaways: Chinese merchants first used paper certificates as money during the Tang Dynasty
The Song Dynasty issued the first government-backed paper currency
Over-issuance by the Yuan Dynasty led to severe inflation and abandonment

faq.question: Why did China invent paper money?
faq.answer: Copper coins were heavy and difficult to transport for large transactions. Merchants in Sichuan Province began using paper certificates backed by coin deposits as a lighter alternative. The government later took over issuance for the entire empire.

faq.question: What happened when China printed too much paper money?
faq.answer: The Yuan Dynasty printed massive amounts to fund military campaigns. The resulting inflation destroyed public trust in paper currency. China largely abandoned paper money for centuries until Western influence brought the concept back.
